name: Bielsa museum – the Bielsa Pocket
story: When the Nationalist Aragon offensive broke the front in spring 1938, the Republican 43rd Division under Antonio Beltrán ('El Esquinazau') was cut off in the high Pyrenean valley of Bielsa. For about two months the division held the 'Bolsa de Bielsa' pocket against far larger forces while thousands of civilians crossed the passes into France. In mid-June 1938 the soldiers followed them. Most of the men went back to Republican Catalonia to keep fighting. Bielsa itself was largely destroyed. The village museum has a section on the pocket and the exodus.
see: A local museum with photographs, documents and objects about the Bielsa Pocket and the flight of civilians over the border.
plan: Museo de Bielsa 'José María Escalona', Plaza Mayor, Bielsa, with a section on the Bielsa Pocket and the exodus. Opening changes with the season, so check before you go or arrange a visit in advance. Bielsa is in the high Pyrenees near the tunnel to France; combine it with a walk in the valley.
